info.title: Intron control plane
info.description:
Configuration and actions for the Intron SIP platform.

**Nothing here is in the path of a call.** The ESL controller carries calls and reads Postgres directly; this API exists so a human or a script can configure the platform and see what it did.

## Authentication

Every endpoint takes `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. Two kinds of key work:

- **`CONTROL_PLANE_API_TOKEN`** from the environment — admin, platform-wide. It has to work before any key exists, including for the request that creates the first one.
- **An API key** from `POST /v1/api-keys` — scoped to a tenant, revocable, stored as a SHA-256 hash and shown exactly once.

## Tenant scoping

A platform key may name any tenant. A tenant-scoped key **always** gets its own, whatever `tenant_id` says — that is what stops the query parameter being a cross-tenant read.

`404` covers both "no such row" and "exists but is not yours", deliberately: answering `403` for the second would confirm it exists.

## Statuses

| | |
|---|---|
| `400` | The body is wrong. **Unknown JSON fields are rejected** — a typo in `recording_mode` would otherwise be silently ignored |
| `401` | No token, or one that is not recognised |
| `403` | Authenticated, but not permitted |
| `409` | The database refused the change because it breaks a rule — numbers already claimed by another trunk or line, a line outside its trunk's numbers, deleting a trunk lines still use. The message says which |
| `429` | The tenant is at its concurrency cap |
| `501` | Deliberately not implemented, e.g. `sip_password` before credential encryption exists |

get.summary: Would a call to this number be admitted?
get.description:
The first thing to check when a client says calls are not arriving. Answered by the **same code the call path uses** — a diagnostic with its own reimplementation of the rules is worth nothing on the day the two disagree.

Answers from this process's cache; the controller's expires independently, so a very recent edit may not have reached a live call yet.

post.description:
Validates, claims a concurrency slot, and **queues** the call. It does not dial: only the ESL controller holds connections to FreeSWITCH, so the handoff is a row claimed with `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` — which also means a queued call survives a controller restart.

`202`, not `201`: nothing has been created that you can use and nobody's phone has rung yet.

status.description: A suspended tenant's calls are refused with CALL_REJECTED (SIP 403).

concurrency_cap.description: Maximum simultaneous calls. Null means no cap — correct for beta, and the wrong default for a platform wired to carriers.

clear_concurrency_cap.description: Removes the cap. Sending null for concurrency_cap leaves it unchanged.

tenant_id.description: Absent means the platform trunk: ours, with its numbers leased to tenants line by line. Set means the client's own (BYOT).

has_password.description: The credential itself is never returned.

signalling_cidrs.description: MUST also be in TF_VAR_carrier_sip_cidrs and applied, or inbound packets are dropped at the security group with nothing logged on the edge.

did_ranges.description: The number inventory: every number a carrier can deliver on this trunk. A number can be on only one trunk — a request claiming numbers another trunk carries is refused with 409.

sip_password.description: REFUSED with 501: credential encryption is not implemented. Accepting it would either store a carrier credential in the clear or silently drop it.

did_ranges.description: The number inventory: every number a carrier can deliver on this trunk. A number can be on only one trunk — a request claiming numbers another trunk carries is refused with 409.

next_steps.description: A trunk is HALF an operation — the other half is Terraform, and nothing enforces the pair.

did_ranges.description: REPLACES the inventory. Refused with 409 if it drops numbers a traffic config still uses.

traffic_config_id.description: Set: an override for that one line. Absent: part of the tenant's default list. A line with any enabled override uses only its overrides.

kind.description: An e164 target is a new outbound call placed over the CALL'S trunk — the one its line's numbers live on. A sip_uri carries its own host.

traffic_config_id.description: Move onto that line's override list.

clear_traffic_config.description: Move back to the tenant's default list.

recording_mode.description: none: do not record. ai_only: record the AI conversation and stop when a human takes over. full: record the whole call, handoff included. Snapshotted when a call starts; editing it does not affect calls in progress.

token.description: Shown ONCE. Only a SHA-256 hash is stored; a lost key is replaced, not recovered.

label.description: Required: 'which key is this and can I revoke it' is the only question ever asked of this table.

scopes.description: A key cannot be issued with a scope its creator does not hold.

NumberRange.description: An inclusive block of E.164 numbers. Both ends must have the same number of digits. A single number is a block whose from and to are equal. Adjacent and overlapping blocks are merged on write and come back merged.

destination.description: Inbound: what happens when the number rings. Outbound: what the answered customer is connected to — reject is refused for an outbound line.
